The area of one loop of the polar curve $r=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(7\theta +\frac{\pi }{2})$ (shown above) is given by the integral

$$
A={\int }_{-\pi /7}^{0}{cos}^{2}⁡(7\theta +\frac{\pi }{2})\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Which of the following represents the total area bounded by the polar curve?
question.worked_solution:
The given polar curve is the polar rose with $7$ petals, and we know that the area of the first petal is

$$
A={\int }_{-\pi /7}^{0}{cos}^{2}⁡(7\theta +\frac{\pi }{2})\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

The $1$st petal is traversed from ${\theta }_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{7}$ to ${\theta }_{2}=0,$ and the length of this interval is $\frac{\pi }{7}.$

To find the interval for the second petal, we have to add $\frac{\pi }{7}$ to both ends of the interval of the first petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{3} & ={\theta }_{1}+\frac{\pi }{7}=-\frac{\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=0 \\ {\theta }_{4} & ={\theta }_{2}+\frac{\pi }{7}=0+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{\pi }{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, to obtain the interval for the third petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{7}$ to both ends of the interval of the second petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{5} & ={\theta }_{3}+\frac{\pi }{7}=0+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{\pi }{7} \\ {\theta }_{6} & ={\theta }_{4}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{2\pi }{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the interval for the fourth petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{7}$ to both ends of the interval of the third petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{7} & ={\theta }_{5}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{2\pi }{7} \\ {\theta }_{8} & ={\theta }_{6}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{2\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{3\pi }{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, to obtain the interval for the fifth petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{7}$ to both ends of the interval of the fourth petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{9} & ={\theta }_{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{2\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{3\pi }{7} \\ {\theta }_{10} & ={\theta }_{8}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{3\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{4\pi }{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the interval for the sixth petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{7}$ to both ends of the interval of the fifth petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{11} & ={\theta }_{9}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{3\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{4\pi }{7} \\ {\theta }_{12} & ={\theta }_{10}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{4\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{5\pi }{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the interval for the seventh petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{7}$ to both ends of the interval of the sixth petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{13} & ={\theta }_{11}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{4\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{5\pi }{7} \\ {\theta }_{14} & ={\theta }_{12}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{5\pi }{7}+\frac{\pi }{7}=\frac{6\pi }{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, we obtain the following intervals for all $7$ petals of our rose:

$$
{{[-\frac{\pi }{7},0]}_{⏟}}_{1\text{st}},\,{{[0,\frac{\pi }{7}]}_{⏟}}_{2\text{nd}},\,{{[\frac{\pi }{7},\frac{2\pi }{7}]}_{⏟}}_{3\text{rd}},\,{{[\frac{2\pi }{7},\frac{3\pi }{7}]}_{⏟}}_{4\text{th}},\,{{[\frac{3\pi }{7},\frac{4\pi }{7}]}_{⏟}}_{5\text{th}}\,{{[\frac{4\pi }{7},\frac{5\pi }{7}]}_{⏟}}_{6\text{th}},\,{{[\frac{5\pi }{7},\frac{6\pi }{7}]}_{⏟}}_{7\text{th}}
$$

Therefore, the total area of the given polar curve can be obtained if the curve is traversed from $\theta =-\frac{\pi }{7}$ to $\theta =\frac{6\pi }{7}:$

$$
{A}_{\text{total}}={\int }_{-\pi /7}^{6\pi /7}{cos}^{2}⁡(7\theta +\frac{\pi }{2})\,\text{d}\theta 
$$
